description: Triage stage for entry-point candidates. Detects entry points in Ariadne packages or external codebases and triages false positives via per-entry investigators, publishing each false positive raw and self-contained.

flows.name: Detect entry-point candidates → per-entry triage → publish v5 triage_results
flows.description: Four-phase pipeline: detect entry points, classify against the known-issues registry, dispatch one investigator per residual candidate, and publish a self-contained v5 triage_results envelope (novel_issues / classifier_regressions / confirmed_unreachable / uncertain).
intentions: Write boundary: triage never writes known_issues/registry.json — it reads the registry only to filter classifier hits; every status transition is a human decision.
Every residual entry gets an investigator verdict — there is no early exit; a registry classifier match is handled upstream in Phase 2 auto-classify, before an investigator is dispatched.
Auto-classify and the investigator's in-scope slice match only wip + permanent registry rows.
Every false-positive verdict is self-contained — it carries its own evidence, so there is no in-run consolidation; offline grouping happens downstream in plan.
Finalize builds the published envelope entirely from the per-entry verdict files in results/, re-parsing each via parse_triage_verdict — a malformed shape halts finalize, never silently skips.
The published envelope is schema v5 — readers hard-reject any triage_results whose schema_version does not match; there are no migration shims.

flows.name: Author a new project detection config
flows.description: When the target is a directory path with no saved config, preview the folder tree, pick exclusions to keep the indexed file count ≤ ~4,000, confirm with the user via AskUserQuestion, and save a project config the rest of the pipeline reads.
intentions: Keep the effective indexed file count ≤ ~4,000; present the full preview list and let the user's final answer be authoritative.
No project configs ship pre-authored — a config is authored only through this reviewed flow.
project_name is auto-derived for external projects; only internal (project_path: ".") projects carry an explicit project_name.

entry.condition: input is a directory path with no saved project config for that path

flows.name: Compare two finalized runs to surface regression candidates
flows.description: Diff two runs' published triage_results to highlight TP↔FP flips, appeared/disappeared entries, group-id changes, and membership deltas. Reads only the published files, so it works even after the underlying run dirs are pruned.
intentions: Diffing reads only the published triage_results/<run-id>.json — it works even when the underlying run dirs have been pruned.
Never mutates any run state — the diff is a read-only comparison.

flows.name: Prune / abandon run directories
flows.description: Garbage-collect old run dirs (prune_runs.ts, default keep 5) and mark in-flight runs abandoned (abandon_run.ts), clearing a stale LATEST pointer.
intentions: Published triage_results/<run-id>.json are kept forever — prune only run dirs, never the analysis_output tree.
Active and abandoned runs never auto-prune; a run referenced as another run's tp_cache.source_run_id is protected.

stores.semantic_role: Canonical classifier registry (wip + permanent + fixed rows). This skill reads it to auto-classify entries and to build the investigator's in-scope wip/permanent slice, but NEVER writes it — every status transition is a human decision applied through atomic_update_registry via the reconcile-registry skill.

Per-run working state: manifest.json (status, commit_hash, tp_cache), triage.json (entries + per-entry results), results/<entry_index>.json (one TriageVerdict per residual entry), and the LATEST pointer to the active run-id. prepare_triage writes LATEST; finalize_triage clears it.
Timestamped detection output, kept project-scoped; one detection feeds many triage runs. prepare_triage reads the latest as its --analysis input.

The published v5 envelope (novel_issues, classifier_regressions, confirmed_unreachable, uncertain). Written by finalize_triage; re-read on the next same-commit run as the TP cache (confirmed_unreachable_reuse), by diff_runs, and by downstream skills. Preserve forever — never rm -rf.
Per-project detection config (project_path, optional folders/exclude, optional project_name). Authored through the config-authoring flow and passed to every phase via --config.

sub_agents.multiplicity: one per residual llm-triage entry; the main agent runs a continuous worker pool that bounds concurrency to N=5 and caps total dispatch at --max-count (default 250)
